enhanced_information: In the treatment of aggressive lymphoma, Rituximab-CHOP is a standard regimen that has shown significant efficacy. Cytoreductive surgery may be beneficial in specific cases to reduce tumor burden before chemotherapy, but it is not universally required. The consensus supports Rituximab-CHOP for 6-8 cycles as an effective initial treatment, with subsequent options depending on response. Retroperitoneal radiotherapy can be considered after chemotherapy in certain cases, but intensive chemotherapy followed by stem-cell transplantation is typically reserved for relapsed or refractory cases. CNS prophylaxis is important in high-risk patients but is not a standalone treatment. Delaying treatment for further imaging (PET-CT) may not be advisable if the patient is symptomatic or has aggressive disease. Therefore, the most appropriate treatment option is likely to be Rituximab-CHOP for 6-8 cycles, potentially followed by radiotherapy or further interventions based on response.
